HOW THIS IS CALCULATED
Pace base. Your race becomes a 5km equivalent with Riegel (time × distance ratio ^ 1.06). Results under 5km are slowed by 8s/km × ln(5 ÷ km). Paces beyond the half marathon are slowed, rising linearly to a marathon slow-down that depends on weekly distance: the marathon is twice the half marathon plus 7 min at 80 miles (129km) a week or more, plus 10 min at 70 miles (113km), 13 at 60, 17 at 50, and 25 at 35 miles (56km) or less. With no weekly distance, 70 miles is assumed. These corrections are my estimates.
Rep pace. Set by rep length and interpolated between anchors: 200m at 91–96% of 5km pace time, 300m at 5km pace ±2s/km, 400m at 8–10km pace, 3 min at 14–16km pace, 6 min at 20–21km, 10 min at 25–30km, tempo reps of 15–20km at 3–6% slower than marathon pace. The 3, 6 and 10 minute anchors follow Copeland's book, as relayed to me. The rest are my estimates.
Recovery. From the rule at each anchor (90s at 200m, 45s at 300–400m, 60s at 3–6 min, 75–90s at 8–10 min, 120s at 12 min, 150–240s at 15–20 min), interpolated. Beyond 20 min it rises from 195s to 300s at 40 min (my estimate).
Suggested reps. My estimate: total work at each anchor ÷ rep time. Sessions are capped at 25km, and at 5km of mile-paced work, 10km of 5km-paced or 400m work, 1 hour of 3–12 min reps and 2 hours of marathon-paced work.
Weekly distance (optional). Caps the top of the range at a share of weekly distance: 5% for 200m, 8% for 300m, 10% for 400m, 12% for 3–12 min reps, 20% for 15 min and longer. These are Daniels' figures except 12%, which I raised from his 10% because most of these sessions are below threshold pace. The lower share applies between anchors. Floors: 2km mile-paced, 4km 5km-paced, 6km slower work.
Session load. TSS = hours × (threshold pace ÷ pace)² × 100. Threshold is the predicted 16km pace. Warm-up and cool-down default to 62.5% of 5km speed (editable), reps run at the middle of the pace range and recoveries are walked at 6km/h.
Treadmill. ACSM running equation: belt speed = flat speed ÷ (1 + 4.5 × grade). Rep times stay the same. It ignores air resistance and treadmill calibration.
Treat all numbers as starting points and check them against heart rate or feel. Keep the last rep within 1–2s per 200m, or 3s per 400m, of the first.

HOW THIS IS CALCULATED
Pace base. The same model as the Race Prediction Calculator: Riegel (time × distance ratio ^ 1.06), a slow-down for results under 5km, and a marathon slow-down that depends on weekly distance. Paces are named for the race distance they match, such as 5k pace: the predicted race pace over that distance. M pace is marathon pace.
Tempo. 20 minutes runs at threshold, the predicted 16km pace. Longer tempos slow down by 4.9% × ln(minutes ÷ 20), never slower than marathon pace, up to 60 minutes. The scale is a fit to a Daniels-style table you supplied (+1.2% at 25 minutes, +5.3% at 60). I have not seen the source of that table.
Ladder. The 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 minute reps run at 10k, 5k, 3k, 2k and 1500m pace. The jog between reps is 90s by default.
Aussie quarters. 400m at 4k pace, then 200m floated at M pace to 3% faster, repeated with no stop. Eight reps is 4.8km, 5km with an opening 200m float.
Mona fartlek. 2×90s, 4×60s, 4×30s and 4×15s, each followed by a float of the same length, as in Nate Jenkins' article on the Moneghetti fartlek. Efforts run at 5k, 4k, 3k and mile pace. The article says about 5k effort for the 90s, getting faster as reps shorten. Floats run at 85% of 5km speed (my choice), about 5s/km slower than marathon pace for an 18:24 runner. The article calls them a quick jog.
Yasso 800s. 800m at 5k pace with a jog of the same time. The old rule (800m time in minutes:seconds = marathon time in hours:minutes) is shown for comparison only.
Rosario 800s. 800m at 5k pace with an 800m float at 5k pace plus 25s per 800m, which is about +31s/km.
1km repeats, mile repeats, 30/30. 1km at 4.5k pace, 1 mile at 10k pace, and 30s at 3k pace with a 30s jog.
Marathon-pace long run. Easy running first, then the chosen distance at marathon pace.
Session load. TSS = hours × (threshold pace ÷ pace)² × 100. Warm-up, cool-down and jogs run at 62.5% of 5km speed unless you change the pace.
The paces are my choices from your descriptions, not published prescriptions. This page does not apply weekly-volume limits. Check the numbers against heart rate or feel.
